bull_bear.body:
- No debt; does not plan to raise debt. Preferential allotment in-principle approval received; funds expected imminently.
- Cash ~INR 20 cr (as of 31-Dec-2025).
- Disciplined: cut low-visibility miniature-bellows outlay, redeploy to demand-backed projects (liquid cooling, hoses, annealing).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- US tariff (50%) — biggest market (US ~55% of exports); blocks new-customer onboarding; bellows ramp delayed.
- Heavy export concentration (74% sales; EU+US ~85% of exports) and single-customer dependence in liquid cooling (5-yr exclusive, India-only).
- Liquid-cooling demand entirely partner-forecast-driven; data-center capex cyclicality.
- Execution: capacity additions across hoses/assemblies/bellows running behind schedule.
- SS raw-material price volatility (partially hedged).
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident but measured ("Q3 good, not very good"); candid on Q1 weakness, bellows being behind schedule, and tariff drag on new customers. Emphasis on long-term margin path and moat narrative.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- Liquid-cooling skid is flow-control IP adaptable beyond data centers (large machinery, semiconductor, HVAC, EV cooling) — collapse-of-DC optionality.
- Partner intends to make the India entity a **global supply hub** for skid assemblies in 3–4 years (exports possible ~6 months out) — large latent upside beyond the India-only INR 350 cr peak.
- Moat = 15–20 yrs flow-control engineering + proprietary flow-simulation software + customer access, not just "changing a hose design."
- Assembly growth is self-reinforcing: more assemblies → more captive hose-braid production.
- India–EU FTA structurally neutralizes Turkish duty-free advantage in EU.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- Global technology partnership with a US-based data-centre infrastructure leader providing early entry and commercial traction in liquid cooling
- Established global customer relationships and export presence across 90+ countries diversified across Americas, Europe and Asia
- Deep innovation pipeline: 58 products under R&D across various stages, including 16 specifically for data-centre liquid cooling
- Engineering differentiation, product quality and customer intimacy cited as basis for competing against new entrants
- Investment in automation and robotic welding lines strengthening throughput and product quality
- Vertical integration and end-to-end fluid-flow capability via Hyd-Air Engineering acquisition, with German technology-enabled capabilities
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export and geopolitical concentration — Geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, tariff measures, sanctions and regional economic disruptions may affect demand, pricing and supply-chain continuity across the Company's 90+ export markets; the ongoing Middle East conflict and residual trade-policy uncertainty add to global fragmentation risk.
- Foreign exchange risk — Currency fluctuations may affect export realisations, profitability and the value of foreign-currency-denominated transactions, given the Company's significant international revenue exposure.
- New product / liquid-cooling adoption risk — In the thermal-management business, the pace of liquid-cooling adoption in Indian data centres remains at an early stage relative to North America and Europe; longer customer qualification cycles, higher initial investment costs for operators and the prevalence of gas-based cooling in India's installed base may moderate the near-term revenue ramp.
- Market and demand risk — Slowdowns in industrial activity, changes in customer spending patterns, competitive intensity and sector-specific demand fluctuations may impact order inflows, capacity utilisation and revenue growth.
- Supply chain risk — Disruptions in raw material availability, logistics bottlenecks or supplier concentration may affect production schedules and customer deliveries.
- Regulatory and compliance risk — Changes in environmental regulations, export controls, trade policies, taxation frameworks and industry-specific standards across domestic and international markets may increase compliance costs or affect market access.
- Operational risk — Manufacturing interruptions arising from equipment failures, process inefficiencies, utility disruptions or human error may impact productivity, quality and customer commitments.
- Technology and cybersecurity risk — Increasing reliance on digital systems exposes the Company to risks related to cyberattacks, data breaches and system failures.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Hoses & assemblies** — core; assemblies (hose+braid) the growth focus, mgmt wants share to keep rising. Capacity +1M meters added this month → 17.5M; → 20M phased by Q2FY27.
- **Metal bellows** — run-rate INR 12 cr; Phase-2 (120k→300k units) deferred until Phase-1 optimal.
- **Miniature metal bellows** — capex cut INR 23 cr → INR 10.5 cr; capacity 240k → ~50–60k units/yr; peak only ~INR 8–9 cr; demand slower than hoped.
- **Liquid cooling (skid assemblies)** — first commercial dispatch done; capacity 2,000 → 15,000 units/yr by Jun-2026; new Chakan (Pune) support plant; capex <INR 100 cr; ~INR 3 lakh/piece realization at 80% utilization. Margins better than hoses, in line with assemblies.
- **Hyd-Air (subsidiary)** — revenue INR 8.5 cr (vs INR 2.9 cr YoY); ~70% utilization; capex planned.

business.body:
- Describes itself as a leading manufacturer of metallic flexible flow solutions with 28 years of industry leadership, 3,300+ SKUs, exports to 90+ countries and a customised-solution model for high-end applications.
- Claims high entry barriers built on engineering-intensive products, strong technical expertise, in-house R&D/customisation and long-standing customer relationships.
- Frames itself as an approved supplier to a leading global provider of digital infrastructure and thermal management solutions, giving access to global and domestic data centre deployments.
- Sells into both traditional sectors (oil & gas, steel, petrochemicals, chemicals/pharma, paper) and emerging ones (data centres, semiconductors, hydrogen, solar, electric mobility, robotics, aerospace & defence).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Governance] Board oversight includes independent directors drawn from the Tata Group, Ashok Leyland and Senior India, with the company under professional management.
- [Digital] Building a connected digital backbone with integrated SAP ERP across finance, inventory and production planning (production lines linked via tablets for real-time machine efficiency) and Salesforce CRM covering lead-to-fulfilment.
- [Ownership] Established in 1998 and acquired in 2018 by Aeroflex Enterprises Limited (formerly Sat Industries Limited).
- [Market] Cites a global liquid cooling market CAGR of 33.2% and direct-to-chip cooling CAGR of 35.0% over CY25-CY32e, plus a 9+ GW announced Indian data centre pipeline over five years led by Reliance Jio, Adani, TCS, CapitaLand, Nxtra, STT GDC India, CtrlS and Yotta.
- [Recognition] Great Place to Work certification 2025-26, 16th CII National HR Excellence Award 2025-26 and EEPC India Export Excellence Awards (Western Region) for 2022-23 and 2023-24; participated in Data Center World Exhibition, USA in April 2026.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Aeroflex Industries manufactures stainless-steel corrugated flexible hoses (with and without braiding), metal bellows and engineered assemblies/fittings used for fluid transfer and flow control across oil & gas, petrochemicals, power generation, fire suppression, ports and terminal handling, chemicals, food and pharmaceutical processing, and solar energy. During FY26 it commercialised SFN liquid-cooling skid assemblies, a plug-and-play closed-loop coolant distribution product for high-density AI/data-centre compute hardware, marking its entry into thermal management for digital infrastructure. Its wholly owned subsidiary Hyd-Air Engineering (Chakan, Pune) makes hydraulic fittings and fluid connectors, serving railways, shipbuilding, defence, steel and heavy machinery.

outlook.title: Growth

outlook.body:
- Expand the liquid-cooling solutions business for data centres and AI infrastructure as a new growth vertical, building on the partnership with a US-based data-centre infrastructure technology leader
- Move up the value chain by increasing the contribution of assemblies and metal bellows relative to standard hose products
- Strengthen automation and advanced manufacturing capabilities (robotic welding lines, automatic welding station, annealing plant, Industry 4.0 / SAP ERP adoption)
- Deepen vertical integration and end-to-end fluid-flow solutions capability through the Hyd-Air Engineering acquisition
- Pursue strategic expansion of international presence, including initiatives in the United States and the Middle East
- Diversify into adjacent growth vectors: hydrogen infrastructure, EV thermal management, HVAC, semiconductors, robotics and automation
- Continue evaluating selective opportunities to enhance capabilities and broaden market reach
- Manage thermal-management adoption risk through phased capacity expansion, active customer engagement and a diversified domestic/international go-to-market approach
- Dividend payments are governed by the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy, framed in accordance with Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations (policy available on the Company's website); the final dividend for FY26 is being recommended for member approval under that policy. Governance policy framework additionally includes Risk Management, Succession, ESOP, Related Party Transaction, Policy on Material Subsidiaries, and Policy for Identification of Material Litigations/Group Companies/Outstanding Dues, indicating a structured, board-governed approach to capital and risk stewardship rather than a stated payout ratio.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Aeroflex pursued capacity expansion on multiple fronts during FY26 and into FY27. SS flexible hose capacity was augmented by 1.0 million metres in Q3FY26 to 17.5 million metres p.a. installed as at 31 March 2026 (~70% utilisation during the year), with a further expansion to 20 million metres p.a. on track for completion by Q2FY27. In the assemblies business, two robotic welding lines were added in Q4FY26 (46 assembly stations as at 31 March 2026), and the Company plans to add more assembly stations together with commissioning an automatic welding station and annealing plant by December 2026. The new SFN liquid-cooling skid assembly line was scaled from 2,000 units p.a. installed capacity in December 2025 to 6,000 units p.a. as at 31 March 2026, with further expansion to 9,000 units targeted in Q2FY27 en route to a total installed capacity of 15,000 units p.a. by Q2FY27. Hyd-Air Engineering (wholly owned subsidiary) upgraded its quality laboratory and R&D centre at Chakan, Pune. The Company also derives benefits from a 750 KW rooftop solar power project installed at its Taloja manufacturing facility (installed in the previous financial year) and operates a NABL-accredited Research & Development Laboratory; during FY26 it incurred R&D expenditure of ₹395.50 lakhs focused on new product development, including liquid-cooling solutions for data centres and AI infrastructure.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's sustained industrial capex cycle (National Infrastructure Pipeline, PM Gati Shakti, PLI schemes) is expanding addressable demand across oil & gas, petrochemicals, refineries, power generation, ports and terminals, and firefighting systems
- Make in India initiative and defence indigenisation (IDDM framework) are opening new addressable markets in aerospace and defence for certified Indian manufacturers
- Structural shift toward liquid cooling in data-centre and AI infrastructure is the most significant medium/long-term opportunity; global liquid-cooling market expected to grow nearly tenfold by 2034 and India's nearly fourteen-fold over the same period
- Energy transition and clean-energy infrastructure (green hydrogen, solar) expanding application of flow-control products in high-purity gas handling and thermal management
- India's emerging semiconductor fabrication and electronics manufacturing base creating demand for ultra-precision vacuum/wafer-handling products
- Rapid EV adoption creating demand for bellows in battery thermal management and cooling
- Diversified end-market presence and strong customer stickiness helping sustain growth momentum despite headwinds in certain export markets
- Domestic market witnessed particularly strong growth driven by project demand across ports, irrigation, oil & gas, petrochemicals and steel sectors
- Increasing adoption of value-added products (assemblies, bellows, liquid-cooling solutions) expected to further strengthen business mix and enhance profitability
- Pace of liquid-cooling adoption in Indian data centres (early-stage relative to North America/Europe) flagged as principal risk moderating near-term revenue ramp for the thermal-management business
- Competitive intensity in both core and new businesses is a continuous risk addressed through engineering differentiation, product quality and customer intimacy
- Aeroflex enters FY27 with a strong outlook, supported by a healthy order pipeline, established customer relationships and a strong balance sheet
- Continuous orders and dispatches under the long-term agreement with the US-based data-centre infrastructure partner reflect the strength of the Company's engineering capabilities and R&D expertise
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Niche, cash-generative SS flexible-flow maker pivoting up the value chain — value-added products (assemblies/fittings/bellows/skids) now 54% of 9M sales — with a new, high-optionality leg in data-center liquid-cooling skid assemblies under a 5-year India-exclusive deal with a US multinational. Highest-ever quarterly revenue/EBITDA/PAT despite a 50% US tariff and an 8% price discount, offset by internal cost engineering and supply-chain sharing.

open.item: Expansion of SFN liquid-cooling skid assembly manufacturing capacity to 9,000 units in Q2FY27, targeting total installed capacity of 15,000 units per annum by Q2FY27
Expansion of SS flexible hose manufacturing capacity to 20 million metres per annum
Added 1 million meters of hose capacity this month to reach 17.5 million meters; balance 2.5 million meters (to 20M) to be commissioned in phases by Q2 of next financial year (FY27)
Planned addition of more assembly stations together with commissioning of an automatic welding station and annealing plant to strengthen assembly throughput and quality
Ongoing process automation (robotic/automated welding stations and an annealing plant) targeted for completion by the end of calendar year 2026
Expect overall EBITDA margins to remain in the range of 23% to 25% over the next couple of years, with a target of reaching 25%
Metal bellows at INR12 crores annual run rate now, expected to increase to ~INR36 crores run rate over the next few quarters; peak (~INR85 cr) by end FY28/start FY29
Overall peak revenue potential across divisions of more than INR1,000 crores over the next 3 years
Liquid cooling skid assembly peak revenue potential of INR300-350 crores at ~80% utilization, expected to be achieved by FY29 (2-2.5 years)
4-5 years out, at least 25% to 30% of business (if not more) expected to come from metal bellows

Continue to evaluate opportunities to strengthen international presence further, including strategic expansion initiatives in the United States, the Middle East and other high-potential global markets
Final dividend of ₹0.40 per equity share (20% of face value ₹2), recommended by the Board for FY26, payable within 30 days of AGM subject to member approval
Long-term objective of increasing the contribution of assemblies to nearly 70-75% of revenues, other than from the liquid-cooling solutions business, over the next few years
US tariff of 50% flagged; company took an 8% price hit/discount; new US customer onboarding delayed though existing customers continue repeat orders
Expect higher traction from EU over next couple of years, boosted by the India-EU FTA improving competitiveness versus Turkey-based players
Hyd-Air running at ~70% capacity utilization; further capex planned to be announced soon; peak revenue potential ~INR45-50 crores
Overall capex including working capital of ~INR97 crores planned; ~INR36 cr already spent in 9M FY26 (INR9 cr liquid cooling, INR5 cr bellows, INR22 cr hoses/assemblies)
Preferential allotment funds expected to be received in the upcoming week (in-principle stock exchange approval received); no debt planned
Hose and assemblies business peak revenue of INR650-675 crores at 20 million meter capacity with 70% assembly mix
Rationalized miniature metal bellows capex from INR23 crores to INR10.5 crores; installed capacity revised from 240,000 to ~50,000 pieces per annum

verdicts.item: Phase 2 capacity expansion to increase hose capacity by additional 3 million meters to 16.5 million meters per annum, to be completed by December 2024
verdicts.note: "We added 1 million meters of hose capacity in this month, which takes our total installed capacity to 17.5 million meters per annum" - the 16.5M milestone has been surpassed.

verdicts.item: Remaining 1.5 million meters of hose capacity to be completed by December 2024, taking total to 16.5 million meters per annum
verdicts.note: "which takes our total installed capacity to 17.5 million meters per annum".

verdicts.item: Metal bellows Phase 1 expected to reach INR85-90 crores top line at 80-90% optimum utilization, in the next year and a half to two years
verdicts.note: "around INR85 crores at peak utilization"; "peak utilization in about 2 years' time from now"; "it is a little behind our schedule".

verdicts.item: Hyd-Air expected to contribute approximately INR30-35 crores of top line by the end of the next financial year (FY26)
verdicts.note: "Hyd-Air, generated revenues of INR8.5 crores in this quarter as compared to approximately INR2.9 crores in the same quarter in the previous year". [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: First automatic assembly welding machine expected to be received by December 2024, to begin automating assembly welding stations
verdicts.note: "process automation, which includes both robotic and automated welding stations... progressing as planned and with the targeted completion by the end of this calendar year".

verdicts.item: Planning a further hose capacity expansion beyond 16.5 million meters, with details/definitive capex plan to be shared in the Q3 FY25 earnings call
verdicts.note: "We added 1 million meters... total installed capacity to 17.5 million meters per annum. The balance 2.5 million meters will be commissioned in a phased manner and is expected to be completed by Q2 of…

verdicts.item: Expanding stainless steel hose and braiding capacity from 16.5 million meters to 20 million meters, projected to be completed by March 2026
verdicts.note: "The balance 2.5 million meters will be commissioned in a phased manner and is expected to be completed by Q2 of the next financial year" - later than the earlier March 2026 target.

verdicts.item: New miniature metal bellows capacity of 240,000 pieces per annum (~20,000/month), estimated completion by March 2026, capex ~INR23 crores
verdicts.note: "we have decided to rationalize the capital expenditure for the Miniature Metal Bellows project from the earlier planned outlay of INR23 crores to INR10.5 crores... revised from 240,000 pieces per ann…

verdicts.item: Plan to increase assembly stations from 40 currently to about 70 within the next 1 year
verdicts.note: "we added 6 new assembly stations, thereby increasing the total number of assembly stations to 46" - short of the ~70 target. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Capex plan from now to March 2026: ~INR54 cr for hose/assembly/welding, ~INR23 cr for miniature bellows, ~INR11.5 cr remaining for Hyd-Air
verdicts.note: "the total capex that we have done across the entire spectrum in this 9 months... is approximately INR36 crores"; "the overall capex, including working capital... is around INR97 crores" - composition…

verdicts.item: Expect 200-300 bps growth in EBITDA margins over the next 2-3 years, reaching about 24% to 25% by FY27 (100 bps/year target)
verdicts.note: "we delivered an EBITDA margin of 23.5%"; "our aim is over the next couple of years to have our margins at up to 25%". [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: At 20 million meters with 70% assembly mix, revenue potential of INR650-675 crores at peak utilization (after ~2 years)
verdicts.note: "at the peak utilization of capacity of 20 million... if 70% of the sales comes from the assemblies, we're expecting a turnover of between INR650 crores to INR675 crores". [±10% rule]

wtt.summary: 33% guidance hit (9 chains); 8/17 projects on-time; 1 expired; 18% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident on a record quarter (23.6% EBITDA margin, 30% export growth) but candid about misses: management admitted metal bellows is 'a little behind our schedule' and cut miniature bellows capex, and owned the tariff-driven 8% price hit and slow new-customer onboarding.
